title: Interpretation of the evidence for the efficacy and safety of statin therapy
authors: Collins R, Reith C, Emberson J, Armitage J, Baigent C, Blackwell L, et al.
funder: not stated; the paper contains no funding statement
authorConflicts: Eight authors work in the Clinical Trial Service Unit, Oxford, which has received research grants from Abbott, AstraZeneca, Bayer, GlaxoSmithKline, Merck, Novartis, Pfizer, Roche, Schering and Solvay under contracts stated to protect its independence, and does not take personal payments from industry; R.C. is co-inventor of a genetic test for statin-related myopathy risk; other authors report grants, consultancy or patents involving Merck, Pfizer, Amgen, Sanofi, Bristol-Myers Squibb and polypill developers.
result: Narrative review by statin trialists. It states that about half of the large statin-against-control trials used a placebo run-in, which the authors argue would not lead to underestimates of side-effect rates, and that a few used an active-drug run-in, which may exclude some patients in whom treatment might cause adverse effects soon after starting. It states that any excesses of muscle-related symptoms due to statin therapy occurred in only about 0.1 to 0.2% of patients each year, that claims of statin intolerance in up to one-fifth of patients rest mainly on reports to regulators and observational studies, and that some reports on statin intolerance were funded by manufacturers of newer lipid-lowering agents.
